answer: The design leans on cross-signed proof-of-personhood, voided if the audit panel is not diverse, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Every claim climbs the vertex of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the shale re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the timber of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
